samples.summary: v1 `PATCH /documents/:documentId` body has no DTO/validation, so a wrong-typed `folderId`/`title` reaches Prisma and surfaces as a 500
samples.evidence: `@Body() body: { title?: string; folderId?: string | null }` is an inline type, not a class, so the global `ValidationPipe` cannot validate it (the new spec comment even says so). A caller sending `folderId: 123`, `folderId: {}` or `title: []` passes `body.folderId !== undefined` and is handed straight to `this.folderService.assertSameWorkspace(body.folderId, workspaceId)` → `prisma.folder.findUnique({ where: { id: <non-string> } })`, and `data.title = <non-string>` → `prisma.document.update`. Prisma raises `PrismaClientValidationError`, which is not an `HttpException`, so the agent-facing route answers 500 with an internal error instead of 400. The sibling controller added in the same change does this correctly: `ApiV1FoldersController.update` takes `UpdateFolderDto` with `@IsUUID()` (packages/backend/src/folder/folder.dto.ts:22-24), so the same malformed input there is a clean 400.

samples.summary: `folders delete` help text understates the blast radius: descendant folders are deleted, not just the named folder
samples.evidence: The command description is `'Delete a folder; its documents return to the workspace root (never deleted)'`, which reads as though nothing but the one folder row is removed. `Folder.parent` is declared `onDelete: Cascade` (packages/backend/prisma/schema.prisma:137), so `FolderService.delete` removes the whole subtree of folders; the backend controller comment (folders.controller.ts:153-154) and the schema registry entry (`'Delete a folder and its descendant folders; …'`, packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts) both say so. The CLI help — the text a human or agent actually reads before running a `destructive` command — is the one place that omits it, so a caller can destroy an entire folder hierarchy believing they removed one folder.

samples.summary: `--format` validation happens before the dry-run branch in `folders list`/`create` but after it in `rename`/`move`/`delete`
samples.evidence: `folders list` (line ~38) and `folders create` (line ~62) call `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` ahead of the `if (opts.dryRun)` branch, while `rename`, `move` and `delete` call it after. So `folders list --dry-run --format bogus` errors while `folders delete <id> --dry-run --format bogus` prints a preview and exits 0 — the same flag combination is validated on some subcommands of one namespace and ignored on others.

samples.summary: `createFolder` silently drops a falsy `--parent`, creating at the root instead of reporting the bad value
samples.evidence: `createFolder(name, parentId?)` does `if (parentId) body.parentId = parentId;`. `wafflebase folders create Q1 --parent ''` therefore posts `{ name: 'Q1' }` and reports success for a folder created at the workspace root, rather than letting the server reject the empty id (`CreateFolderDto.parentId` is `@IsUUID()`, so a non-empty bad value would 400). The dry-run preview in commands/folders.ts uses the same `parent ? … : {}` test, so it agrees with the wrong request.
